title: Distance Between Two Points
seo_title: Grade 8 Distance on the Coordinate Plane Worksheets (TEKS 8.7D, STAAR)
standard_text: 8.7D determine the distance between two points on a coordinate plane using the Pythagorean Theorem
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 worksheets for Texas TEKS 8.7D: distance between two points on the coordinate plane with right triangles and the Pythagorean theorem, shapes and maps. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Draw a right triangle and use a² + b² = c².
body_html:
How to think about it

  • For points on the same horizontal or vertical line, the distance is the difference of the coordinates that change.
  • Otherwise, draw a right triangle: the legs are the change in x and the change in y.
  • Use the Pythagorean theorem: d = √((change in x)² + (change in y)²).
  • With negative coordinates, count the units across 0.

Examples

Example

(1, 2) and (4, 6)

Across 3, up 4

√(9 + 16)

Answer: 5

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding the changes: 3 + 4 = 7The distance is the hypotenuse: √(9 + 16) = 5.
Forgetting the square rootd² = 25 means d = 5.
Subtracting with mixed signsFrom −2 to 4 is 6 units.

faq.a: Determine the distance between two points on a coordinate plane using the Pythagorean Theorem.

faq.q: Do I need the distance formula?
faq.a: No. Drawing a right triangle and using a² + b² = c² works every time.
No. Distance is always positive or zero.

faq.q: What if the answer is not a whole number?
faq.a: Leave it as a square root or round it, such as √20 ≈ 4.5.
